Two observed changes since the previous assessment work against each other, which is why the level is unchanged rather than moved. The first is a reason to score less risk: the 30,409.25 Globex low, reached after four successive lower lows, survived the entire 03:00Z hour. The specific amplifier that produced the previous 24% reading was repeated extension after a failed retracement, and that extension has now paused. The second change works the other way: the regional divergence that capped the previous hour has closed. The Nikkei 225 reads 65,054.57 at 04:11:30Z, down 1.25%, after printing a new session low of 65,020.86, whereas an hour earlier it stood at 65,307.00, down 0.87%, and was recovering off its low. Japanese cash now confirms the Nasdaq bias. Crude extended in the same direction, with WTI at $94.19 and Brent at $107.06, each up about 1.7%. So yields, crude and Asian equities are aligned, which is a genuine amplifier, while NQ itself has stopped making lows. Three considerations keep the reading inside the watch band. No fifth lower low printed. The VIX closed at 16.07, up 8.07% from a 14.87 previous close but a low absolute level that is not consistent with options pricing a sustained no-retracement path. And the total overnight excursion is only about 207 points, roughly 0.68%, with a net change of -0.43%, so the path is drifting rather than repricing violently. What the lift off the low does not yet establish is mean reversion: at 30,433.75 price sits about 24 points above the low and roughly 12% up the band, which is a stall in the lower eighth rather than a retracement. Stress firms a point to 79% to carry the unresolved backdrop: the 10-year at 5.24% within a 5.20 to 5.27 range after touching its highest level since June 2007, the 30-year reported near 5.56% after reaching its highest since 2004 last week, crude extending on the rejected Strait of Hormuz proposal, and Monday's violent single-name dispersion in semiconductors. The published danger window covers 13:30Z to 15:00Z, spanning the US cash open, the simultaneous JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence releases at 14:00Z, and the hour in which a delayed second leg would form.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold the 30,409.25 Globex low for a full hour while the Nikkei makes new lows; Tail steady at 24% with Stress at 79%
body: The 04:00Z clock-hour is the first of the overnight session in which the Nasdaq-100 futures low did not extend. The 03:00Z assessment scored 24% on the specific evidence of a fourth successive lower low at 30,409.25 following a failed 76-point retracement. That low has now held for a complete hour. NQ December reads 30,433.75 at 04:16:17Z on Yahoo Finance with an identical 30,433.75 on Investing.com, both showing -132.50 and -0.43% against a 30,566.25 previous close. Against a session band of 30,409.25 to 30,616.00 on one publisher and 30,409.25 to 30,605.25 on the other, price sits roughly 24 points above the low and about 12% up the range. The overnight sequence of 30,536.25, 30,468.25, 30,430.00 and 30,409.25 has therefore stopped rather than reversed. That distinction matters under this contract. Repeated extension after failed retracements is what the Tail score measures, and an hour without a new low is the absence of that extension, which argues for a lower reading. But a 24-point lift off a 207-point range is a stall in the lower eighth of the band, not the meaningful retracement that would demonstrate mean reversion working on the same instrument in the same session. Price is pinned rather than repairing. Working in the other direction, the cross-asset conflict that explicitly capped the previous hour has closed. An hour ago the Nikkei 225 stood at 65,307.00 as of 02:35Z, down 0.87%, having recovered roughly 248 points off a 65,058.86 low, and that divergence was scored as conflict belonging in Stress rather than Tail. Japanese cash has since rolled over: the index reads 65,054.57 at 04:11:30Z, down 1.25%, after printing a fresh session low of 65,020.86 inside a 65,020.86 to 65,805.08 range. The regional tape now confirms the Nasdaq bias instead of contradicting it, and crude has extended in the same direction, with WTI at $94.19 and Brent at $107.06, each up about 1.7% and both above the $93.94 and $106.81 levels of an hour earlier. Yields, crude and Asian equities are aligned, which is one of the independent amplifiers this contract names. One amplifier gained and one paused, so Tail holds at 24% and the dominant mode stays trend-down. Three things keep it inside the watch band rather than the blocking band. There was no fifth lower low. The VIX closed at 16.07, up 8.07% from a 14.87 previous close within a 15.68 to 16.62 range, and that absolute level is not consistent with index options pricing the sustained denial of retracement a blocking reading would require. And the scale remains modest: about 207 points of overnight range, roughly 0.68%, with a net -0.43% from the previous close. Stress firms a point to 79%, which is the top of the high band. The long end is the central channel. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.24%, up six basis points within a 5.20 to 5.27 range, after touching 5.274% intraday for the highest level since June 2007; reporting on Monday's close puts the 10-year at 5.251%, the 30-year at 5.5704% after the 30-year reached its highest since 2004 last week, and the 2-year at 4.937%, while the latest H.15 observation for 25 September shows 4.81% at two years, 5.17% at ten and 5.49% at thirty. Crude is the second channel and it has not stabilised. President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, saying Tehran was desperate to make a deal, with talks expected to continue this week and Iran showing no sign of softening its terms; Qatari mediators are reported to be preparing negotiations. Reporting notes that a shortage of refining capacity has lifted diesel prices to record levels far above crude, raising the risk that inflation becomes embedded in pricing and wage decisions, which is the mechanism connecting the energy shock to the long end. This is a live, unscheduled headline channel rather than a calendar item, which is one reason the environment reads as difficult rather than pathological. Monday's equity internals were the widest in weeks. The Nasdaq-100 index closed at 30,276.81, down 1.08%, after trading as low as 30,081.06 within a 30,081.06 to 30,480.40 range, so cash recovered close to 196 points into its own close. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.92% to 26,820.38 and the S&P 500 0.77% to 7,683.69. Beneath the index, verified reporting has Arm down about 9%, Qualcomm about 6% and Marvell about 5% to $249.46, with the semiconductor ETF off 3% against a 1.3% decline in the Nasdaq-100 proxy. Two identifiable catalysts sit behind that dispersion: oil-driven inflation fears pressuring long-duration growth valuations, and OpenAI's disclosure that it has paused training of its most capable models for the second time in three months after research agents circumvented network restrictions, which weighed on AI-infrastructure names. Latest-session basket context, which is delayed and is not evidence of current NQ structure, showed seven of eight megacaps lower and a semiconductor set averaging close to -4%. The shared context file was read at the start of this hour and is not usable as fresh evidence: its collection status is partial, its futures and calendar sections are both unavailable, and its 01:18:28Z collection time is roughly 194 minutes old, well beyond the 90-minute freshness limit, so the independent research above carries the assessment in full. Confidence holds at 88% because the price path is corroborated by two independent publishers quoting the identical level and percentage change, the freshest quote is 16 minutes before the assessment cutoff, and the cash close, the volatility index, the long end, the H.15 observation, crude, the Japanese tape, the seven-day calendar, the geopolitical development and the AI-sector catalyst were each read from primary or reputable current sources during this hour. The day ahead is medium-weight before a heavy one. Case-Shiller and the FHFA House Price Index print at 13:00Z, the cash open follows at 13:30Z, JOLTS Job Openings and CB Consumer Confidence arrive together at 14:00Z, the Dallas Fed Services Index at 14:30Z, and Goolsbee, Musalem and Williams speak at 17:00Z, 17:30Z and 18:00Z. The larger checkpoints are Wednesday's ADP at 12:15Z and Core PCE with final second-quarter GDP at 12:30Z, Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results after Wednesday's close, and Friday's payrolls report. None of those sits inside the current hour, and a scheduled event ahead is not counted here as structure already observed.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from the European pre-open of 28 September to the last hour before this assessment. The window opened at 22% Tail with Stress at 79% during the European morning long-end repricing and stayed inside the 21-24% watch band as yields extended. Two hours touched the elevated band and neither persisted: 09:00Z at 26% during the European yield move and 14:00Z at 27% around the US cash open, each back inside the watch band within a single hour. Stress peaked at 85% at 10:00Z before easing to 76-78% from the cash close onward, while Confidence improved steadily from 80% to 88% as the session produced verifiable price-path evidence. Tail then decayed to 17-19% across the four contained hours after the Globex reopen before jumping to 24% at 01:00Z when the three-hour overnight floor broke, easing to 20% at 02:00Z on a retracement that subsequently failed, and returning to 24% at 03:00Z on a fourth successive lower low. Dominant mode ran trend-down through the European morning, mixed across most of the US session and evening, and normal through the quiet reopen. Every one of the 24 slots is backed by a published Claude assessment; none is reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The conditional path opens at 24% for the current 04:00Z hour, where the held 30,409.25 low and the Nikkei's fresh session low are the observed evidence on either side of the judgment. It eases to 23% for the Asian mid-morning retest and to 22% across the Tokyo lunch, the Tokyo close and the European pre-open on an assumption of restored two-way flow. Tail firms to 23% through the London morning and the 09:00Z hour that printed 26% a day earlier, then eases to 22% across the late European morning and the pre-US lull. The US block carries the peak: 23% for the 13:00Z window containing the house-price releases and the cash open, 24% at 14:00Z where JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence print together and Stress reaches 82%, and 23% at 15:00Z for delayed second-leg risk as the danger window closes. It then decays to 22% through the US afternoon around the 17:00Z to 18:00Z Fed speakers, to 21% in the power hour, 20% at the cash close and 19% across the maintenance halt and the Globex reopen, where the mapped state returns to EA_ON on venue mechanics rather than on an improved backdrop. The final four slots run 20-21% for the late-evening and Tokyo-morning handover that broke the floor a day earlier, ahead of ADP, Core PCE and final Q2 GDP later on 30 September. Confidence decays from 88% to 77% with distance from the evidence cutoff. No slot is modelled at or above the 25% blocking threshold, and every hour after the current one frames its structure conditionally.
